title: Scientists Create Bananas That Stay Yellow Longer
paragraphs: Have you ever peeled a banana and found that it quickly turned brown? Scientists in the UK have created a new banana that stays yellow for much longer.

The banana was developed by Tropic, a British biotechnology company. The scientists used a gene-editing tool called CRISPR to switch off a gene that produces an enzyme called polyphenol oxidase. This enzyme causes bananas to turn brown when they are peeled, cut or bruised. Without it, the inside of the banana stays yellow for up to 12 hours after peeling. The banana also does not turn brown as easily when it is handled roughly.

The company did not add DNA from other living things. Instead, it changed genes that the banana already had. Because of this, some people believe that it may be easier for governments and shoppers to accept the banana.

According to Tropic, the new banana could help reduce food waste. Bananas go bad very quickly, and according to the UN's Food and Agriculture Organization, a large share of the world's bananas is lost every year. In the UK, a 2017 government survey found that people throw away 1.4 million bananas that are still good to eat every day.
Tropic claims that its banana could cut banana waste in half. However, these figures come from the company itself, and they have not been checked by independent experts.

The banana has already been approved in several countries, including the Philippines, the US, Canada, Japan and Brazil. According to the company, it is expected to go on sale to shoppers in the US and Canada in 2026.
